name: parse-views
title: Parse views
description: A document as Conare read it, three ways: Page beside text (the page and the dark window of what was read, joined by pointing; it ships), Regions (every region numbered with its OCR confidence) and Plain or Conare (a plain reader's text and Conare's, one handle between).

files.content:
'use client' import { ParseOutput } from '@/components/product/ParseOutput' import { ParsePlain } from '@/components/product/ParsePlain' import { ParseRegions } from '@/components/product/ParseRegions' import { ParseSheet } from '@/components/product/ParseSheet' import { useParsePoint, type ParseAnswer } from '@/hooks/useParse' import { Count } from '@/components/ui/Count' import { cn } from '@/lib/cn' // A file as Conare read it (parse/Reading.vue), three ways. 1 "Page beside text" (the one that ships): the page on the // paper beside the dark window of what was read, with four facts over it (how long, regions, tables, OCR; the counts // roll up as they land), joined by pointing. 2 "Regions": the page's structure, every region numbered with its // confidence. 3 "Plain or Conare": a plain reader's text and Conare's on the same page, one handle between them. export interface ParseReadingProps { answer: ParseAnswer version?: 1 | 2 | 3 /** The root's data-ds (a page built on this one says its own, as Vue's fallthrough does). */ 'data-ds'?: string } export function ParseReading({ answer, version = 1, 'data-ds': ds = 'parse-reading' }: ParseReadingProps) { const { setOn, lit, pick } = useParsePoint() const p = answer.part const tables = p.blocks.filter(b => b.type === 'table').length const facts: Array<{ label: string, value: string, count?: number }> = [ { label: 'Read in', value: `${(answer.took_ms / 1000).toLocaleString('en-US', { maximumFractionDigits: 1 })} s` }, { label: 'Regions', value: '', count: p.blocks.length }, { label: 'Tables', value: '', count: tables }, { label: 'OCR', value: p.ocr ? `${Math.round((p.confidence ?? 0) * 100)}% sure` : 'Not needed' }, ] if (version === 2) return if (version === 3) return return (

{answer.name}{`Page ${answer.page} of ${answer.pages}`}

{facts.map((f, i) => (
0 && 'border-code-edge md:border-l', i % 2 === 1 && 'max-md:border-l', i > 1 && 'max-md:border-t')}>
{f.label}
{f.count != null ? : f.value}
))}
) } export default ParseReading

'use client' import { Table } from '@/components/ui/Table' import { ParseSheet } from '@/components/product/ParseSheet' import { REGION, tableOf, useParsePoint, type ParseAnswer, type ParseBlock } from '@/hooks/useParse' // Parse, "Regions" (parse/Regions.vue): the page's structure is the result. The page in the double rule with every // region outlined and numbered, beside a table of the regions in reading order, what each is and how sure OCR was; the // least sure (under 80%) in red, so a reader sees at once what to check by hand. Pointing joins the two. export interface ParseRegionsProps { answer: ParseAnswer 'data-ds'?: string } const preview = (b: ParseBlock) => (b.type === 'table' ? `${tableOf(b.content).rows.length} rows, ${tableOf(b.content).head.length} columns` : b.content.split('\n')[0]!) const UNSURE = 0.8 export function ParseRegions({ answer, 'data-ds': ds = 'parse-regions' }: ParseRegionsProps) { const { setOn, pinned, lit, pick } = useParsePoint() const part = answer.part const unsure = part.blocks.filter(b => b.conf != null && b.conf < UNSURE).length return ( <>

{part.blocks.length} regions in reading order

{part.ocr ? (unsure ? `${unsure} to check by hand` : 'All read clearly') : 'Read from the text layer, no OCR needed'}

{part.ocr && } {part.blocks.map(b => ( setOn(b.order)} onPointerLeave={() => setOn(null)} onClick={() => pick(b.order)}> {part.ocr && } ))}
OrderRegionTextOCR
{b.order} {REGION[b.type] ?? b.type} {b.conf == null ? '' : `${Math.round(b.conf * 100)}%`}
) } export default ParseRegions const css = ` .ds-table tbody tr.ds-parse-on td { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ds-color-surface-accent) 6%, transparent); } `
